title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.6): L is an ambient set and Φ ⊂ P(L) a family of subsets with support |Φ| = ∪Φ. For A ∈ Φ the boundary is ∂_Φ A = ∪{B ∈ Φ : B ⊊ A} and the interior is A° = A \ ∂_Φ A. Φ is *preadmissible* if every x ∈ |Φ| lies in a smallest member A(x) of Φ. It is *admissible* if, in addition, every A° is nonempty. The relation R_Φ ('x ~ y iff A(x) = A(y)') then partitions |Φ| into the strata A°, and each member satisfies A = ∪_{B⊂A} B°. In modern terms, the map x ↦ A(x) is a surjection |Φ| → Φ onto a poset. Its fibres are the strata, and members of Φ are preimages of principal down-sets. So an admissible family is a set stratified by a poset, like the face poset of a regular cell complex, and |Φ| carries the topology pulled back from the Alexandrov (down-set) topology of Φ.

A subfamily Ψ ⊂ Φ is 'fermée' if it is a down-set (a sieve): A ∈ Ψ, B ∈ Φ, B ⊂ A ⇒ B ∈ Ψ.

First proposition (begun on p.6). For Ψ ⊂ Φ the following are equivalent: (a) Ψ is closed in Φ, i.e. |Ψ| is R_Φ-saturated and closed; (b) Ψ is admissible and R_Ψ is the restriction of R_Φ to |Ψ|; (d) the down-closure condition.

On this page Grothendieck proves b ⇒ d. Take A ∈ Ψ, B ∈ Φ, B ⊂ A. B° ≠ ∅ by admissibility of Φ. B° is an R_Φ-class contained in A ⊂ |Ψ|, so by (b) it is an R_Ψ-class, i.e. B° = C° for some C ∈ Ψ. Then B = C, hence B ∈ Ψ.

He then names such Ψ the 'admissible subfamilies'. A scholium notes that they correspond to closed parts of the poset Φ, equivalently to closed saturated parts of |Φ|. They are stable under arbitrary ∪ and ∩, i.e. they form the lattice of down-sets, which is the Alexandrov topology.

Second proposition (gluing). Let Φ, Ψ ⊂ P(L) both be admissible. The following are equivalent:
- (a) Φ ∪ Ψ is admissible and Φ, Ψ are admissible (closed) subfamilies of it; equivalently (a') Φ and Ψ are admissible subfamilies of some admissible family Σ.
- (b) Φ ∩ Ψ is closed in Φ and in Ψ, and |Φ| ∩ |Ψ| = |Φ ∩ Ψ|.
- (c) T = |Φ| ∩ |Ψ| is closed-saturated in |Φ| and in |Ψ|, and for every A ⊂ T, A ∈ Φ ⇔ A ∈ Ψ.

A margin note links this to a condition 'ΦΨ' (stability under intersection).

Proof plan: a' ⇔ a is immediate; a ⇒ b, c was noted earlier. Here he starts b ⇒ c; it is continued on p.8 together with c ⇒ a. On p.8 he shows that for x ∈ T the two minimal members A_Φ(x) and A_Ψ(x) both lie in T, hence belong to both families, hence coincide. This is exactly the classical criterion that two cell or simplicial complexes in a common ambient set glue to a complex iff they meet in a common subcomplex. The whole page serves the foundations of an 'algebra of figures': polyhedral or cellular decompositions treated combinatorially as stratified sets.
errors: In b ⇒ d the step 'B° = C° implies B = C' is asserted without proof. It needs an argument, because under (b) C° is a priori the Ψ-interior, not the Φ-interior. The argument: x ∈ B° gives B = A_Φ(x) ⊂ C. If B ⊊ C, pick y ∈ C°_Φ (nonempty by admissibility of Φ). Then y ∉ B, so y ∈ ∂_Ψ C ⊂ ∂_Φ C, which is a contradiction. So the claim is true but the gap is real.

The first line announces 'Il reste à voir que c) ⟹ b)' but then proves b) ⟹ d). The labels of the first proposition are inconsistent across pp.6–7 (the conditions c), d) are not legibly stated on p.6). This is a bookkeeping slip, not a mathematical one.
In the second proposition, statement a)/a') is heavily reworked with crossings-out; the final intended form appears to be 'Φ, Ψ are admissible subfamilies of an admissible family Σ'.

ideas.what: Admissible subfamily = down-closed subfamily of the poset Φ, characterised equivalently by the induced equivalence relation (strata) being the restricted one
ideas.modern_name: Subcomplex / closed union of strata in a poset-stratified set (Alexandrov topology on a poset)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Alexandrov 1937 for poset topologies; regular CW complexes and face posets: Whitehead, Björner)

ideas.what: Scholium: admissible subfamilies form a lattice stable under arbitrary unions and intersections, matching closed saturated subsets of |Φ|

Gluing criterion: Φ ∪ Ψ is admissible with Φ, Ψ as subfamilies iff Φ ∩ Ψ is a common closed subfamily with |Φ ∩ Ψ| = |Φ| ∩ |Ψ| (equivalently, the intersection of supports is closed in both and the two families agree on subsets of it)
ideas.modern_name: Union of two (cell/simplicial) complexes along a common subcomplex

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful but elementary foundations: poset-stratified sets, subcomplexes, and gluing along a common subcomplex. This is standard combinatorial topology, written out in Grothendieck's own 'figures' vocabulary. The only mild interest is historical: it documents the axiomatic starting point of his 1986 'algèbre des figures', which is related to the tame-topology / dévissage programme of the Esquisse. No new result is on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the image reads 'Il reste à voir que c) ⟹ b)' (or possibly 'a) ⟹ b)'); what follows is 'prouvons l'inverse, supposons b), prouvons d)'. The proof actually given is b ⟹ d.
In the second proposition the struck line reads approximately 'a') Φ et Ψ sont sous-familles adm. d'une famille adm. Σ'. The superscript insertion near Σ looks like 'adm.' (circled), not 'Φ-fermée'.
'[-dans-] Ψ' in a') belongs to a reworked phrase reading roughly 'Φ-finie[?] dans Φ et dans Ψ'. The crossing-outs make the exact wording uncertain.
The insertion '(aux variétés des sol. d'ordre[?])' is doubtful; it more plausibly reads '(aux ensembles ... d'ordre)', referring to order ideals (down-sets) of Φ.
In b) the word is 'Φ-fermé' in the sense of 'fermé' (closed); 'Φ∩Ψ est fermé dans Φ et dans Ψ'.
